title: Event-sourced batch telemetry and KV "grace reaper" to reduce fragmentation and stale-cache burden
creator: Emily Chen
description:
Problem: The continuous-batcher state and KV cache maintenance paths are tightly coupled and emit high-cardinality transient telemetry. This contributes to heap fragmentation on long-lived runtimes, noisy GC, and delayed eviction of stale KV entries (hotkey churn).

Goal: Refactor runtime telemetry to an event-sourced model and introduce a controlled background "grace reaper" for KV shards that reduces live-set churn, lowers p99 tail latency, and cuts memory overhead without hurting steady-state throughput.

Scope:
- Introduce an append-only, per-shard event log for batch lifecycle events (enqueue/commit/drain) used only for telemetry and post-hoc analysis.
- Decouple telemetry collection from the hot path so batching threads do minimal write-amortized operations.
- Implement KV "grace reaper": a background coordinator that marks candidates and reclaims entries only after a tunable grace window, batching deletions to avoid IO bursts.
- Tune allocator/jemalloc runtime knobs and upgrade tokio to 1.30 to get scheduler improvements observed in upstream.
- Add benchmarks, unit/integration tests, and a canary rollout plan with runtime feature gates.

Non-goals: Full redesign of admission control or prefetching strategies. We will not change model-routing logic in this ticket.
comments: 2025-01-09 - Emily Chen: Wrote initial design doc; flagged trade-offs between synchronous vs. append-only log for telemetry. Synchronous writes hurt latency; chosen approach: lock-free ring buffer to append event references and a background spooler to write canonically to per-shard logs.

2025-01-16 - Marcus Alvarez: Prototype of event ring buffer landed in local branch. Microbenchmarks show <1% steady-state throughput regression, p99 improved by reducing allocation churn. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3420

2025-01-22 - Perf: Ran workload B (multi-tenant qps/latency mix). Observed 12% reduction in steady-state heap RSS and 18% reduction in tail latency for short bursts when event buffering is enabled. Need larger scale test for KV reaper impact.

2025-01-30 - Design review (pm+sec+eng): Decided to gate KV grace reaper behind runtime flag and conservative default grace window of 90s. Security requested audit log hooks for deletions (added to scope).

2025-02-03 - Marcus Alvarez: Implemented kv-grace-reaper v1. Behavior: mark candidates on threshold, wait grace window, then reclaim in batch-of-N with backoff. Local integration tests passing. Added metrics: reaper.marked, reaper.reclaimed, reaper.batch_size_histogram.

2025-02-06 - QA: Found intermittent stall in shard compaction under high eviction rate. Root cause: compaction held allocator mutex while iterating tombstones. We introduced per-shard compaction yields and limited per-sweep wall time to 200ms to avoid long pauses.

2025-02-10 - Performance: Upgraded tokio from 1.26 -> 1.30 in a feature branch. Observed scheduler latency benefits under synthetic tasks; no regressions in runtime tests. Dependencies updated in cargo.lock in PR #3456.

2025-02-13 - Security: Audit hooks added to reaper path. Security reviewer (R. Patel) approved minimal-surface approach; flagged retention policy questions for legal. Added follow-up ticket for retention settings (PM to own).

2025-02-15 - Marcus Alvarez: Canary rollout started on two dev clusters (canary-1 & canary-2) behind runtime flag. Early telemetry shows reduced GC churn, 9% lower average RSS, and smoother p95/p99 during traffic spikes. Monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/serving/batcher-kv-memory?view=canary-214789
